subject: Possible issue with initialization (cmdstan and rstan)

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Possible issue with initialization (cmdstan and rstan)
parts:
Hi,

I am experiencing some issues with initialization, both in CmdStan and RStan.

The model is a logistic growth model for a nut with adjustments to the asymptote and log rate constant by cultivar and site (attached w/ example data).

When the parameters are given a prior in a centered parameterization tighter than ~ normal(0, 1), during initialization the parameter is sometimes initialized very far away from the prior (e.g., prior is ~normal(0, 0.1), parameter is initialized at a value of 2), which causes the model to get stuck in an area of low probability.  Restricting the initialization values helps in some cases, but then causes parameters with priors wider than ~ normal(0, 1) to become stuck. Re-parameterizing the priors to a non-centered parameterization solves all issues and results in sampling to proceed well on all chains. 

The reason I thought I should write this is that I originally ran this model over a year ago with the centered parameterization on Stan/Rstan 2.6 with no initialization issues what-so-ever.  However, on 2.12 at least one chain of four does not initialize properly.

For reference, I am currently running this on:
Arch Linux - 4.8.4
GCC - 6.2.1
R - 3.3.1
Cmdstan - 2.12.0
RStan - 2.12.1

Thanks,

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible issue with initialization (cmdstan and rstan)
parts:
We changed how the basic sampling works in NUTS, moving
from a slice sampler to a multinomial sampler, which in
general, has been more robust and less variable across
chains. Sorry to hear it's gone the opposite way for
your problem. This may just be that Stan's gotten better
at diagnosing a pathology in the model that was always
there.

You might want to try a lower stepsize initially if it's
getting stuck during warmup and a larger adapt_delta if
it gets stuck during sampling.

It generally helps to rescale all the parameters. So if
you have:

theta ~ normal(0, 0.1)

then instead take theta_raw as the parameter, modeled as

theta_raw ~ normal(0, 1);

with a transformed parameter or local variable rescaling:

theta = 0.1 * theta_raw;

That is just the non-centered parameterization for a fixed scale
(the non-centering is around 0 for the the mean and the sd on the
log scale).

- Bob

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible issue with initialization (cmdstan and rstan)
parts:
Thus, I could replace every foo ~ normal(mu, sigma) 

by 

(foo - mu) / sigma ~ normal(0, 1); 

given that mu and sigma is not a parameter, there would no jacobian adjustment needed.
Which leads to the question why there is no 

(foo - mu) / sigma ~ standard_normal();

(Hopefully this is not a too silly question)

Andre

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible issue with initialization (cmdstan and rstan)
parts:
It would be confusing, but yes, you could do that.

What you want to look at is what the final target log
density is. That's all that matters up to an additive
constant that doesn't depend on parameters.

I've thought about adding a unit_normal() distribution
just for efficiency --- it avoids a bunch of basic arithmetic
additions of zero and divisions and multiplications by one.
It's just a matter of the resources to do it. Feel free
to make a pull request for that.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible issue with initialization (cmdstan and rstan)
parts:
Another option would be to do what R does with its normal distribution, which is that if mu and sigma are not supplied, it defaults to unit_normal. I for one would not mind a normal distribution that works this way in Stan, thus y ~ normal(); is same as y ~ normal(0,1); and normal_lpdf(y) is the same as normal_lpdf(y|0,1); and so on.
A
